props.title: Flue agent output lifecycle audit — Telegram tasks (incidents B–D)

props.content:
Job: make delivery semantics and artifact lifetimes obvious to an operator. This page demonstrates where the ledger marks completion, where Telegram/GitHub delivery occurs (best-effort), what is lost at sandbox teardown, and which focused tests will reveal these failures.

Short gist:
- The app marks durable completion (ledger.completeTask / ledger.completeGeneralTask) before attempting outbound delivery. Notification failures are logged but do not revert completion (src/tools/task-tools.ts:323-344; 398-424).
- General-task artifacts live only inside the sandbox and are destroyed on completion (src/telegram/files.ts:23-46; src/tools/task-tools.ts:398-424). Recoverability is therefore not possible unless artifacts are persisted to durable storage before destroy.
- Routing: inbound dedupe and conversation isolation are enforced, but natural-language repair requests currently start new tasks rather than read the latest completed task.

props.code:
flowchart LR
  Draft[Draft collection]
  Draft --> Run[run interpretation]
  Run --> Enqueue[enqueue intake work item]
  Enqueue --> Queue[TASK_QUEUE]
  Queue --> Dispatch[Agent dispatch]
  Dispatch --> TerminalTool[Agent calls terminal tool]
  TerminalTool --> LedgerComplete[ledger.completeTask or completeGeneralTask]
  LedgerComplete --> Notify[sendTelegramMessage and sendDocument]
  Notify --> Destroy[sandbox.destroy]
  Dispatch --> AgentNarration[agent ends without terminal tool]
  AgentNarration --> PossibleFail[observer marks failed and destroy]
